what: Negative guards lexically inside a loop over the corpus. A guard here decides what a corpus-wide fix REACHES, which is how the reading-order rollout's `zero paper sections` silently dropped three live pages.
not_a_verdict: Each entry is a CANDIDATE. Many are correct. The ratchet exists so the next one is seen when it is written.

baselined_with_reason.scripts/lint_arm_roles_contradict_the_ob: `if not arms` IS the property meant. A trial with no arms is UNREAD, and the guard increments trials_unread before continuing rather than dropping the row silently -- the absence is counted and reported as a third state, which is the opposite of the reading-order rollout's defect.

`if not named` skips a trial-name segment containing no classifiable word, e.g. 'vs 2'. Nothing is excluded from a fix: the row continues to checks A and C, and only this one comparison is unavailable.
baselined_with_reason.ssot/apply_container_repr_2026_08_20.py:: `if not DICT_IN_TEXT.search(raw): continue` -- the absence IS the property meant. An object with no embedded dict repr has nothing for this pass to repair, and skipping it is not an exclusion from a fix, it is the fix having no work there. The repaired count is reported per object, so a skipped object is visible as a zero rather than as a silence.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/lint_object_write_is_atomic.py:1: The guard records the file as UNPARSED and continues -- it is the three-state path, not an exclusion. A file this checker cannot parse is reported in its own count and named in the output, which is the opposite of dropping it from a corpus-wide pass.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/prove_no_value_lost.py:87: `if not raw: continue` -- the absence IS the property meant, and it is now COUNTED AND NAMED rather than skipped. `raw` empty means `git show HEAD:<path>` returned nothing, i.e. the object has no committed prior state, so it cannot have lost a value against one. The topic is appended to `new_at_head` and printed under its own heading beside the comparison count, so the output states OBJECTS ON DISK, OBJECTS COMPARED, and NOT COMPARED as three numbers a reader can reconcile. Same shape as lint_object_write_is_atomic.py:153. The gate found this while the guard was still a silent `continue` -- at that point the exclusion was real but LATENT: measured, 155 on disk, 155 compared, 0 excluded, so the `0 values lost across 155 objects` already reported was over the whole population. It was true and it was not known to be true.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/prove_abstract_argument_is_never: `if a is None: continue` -- the absence IS the property meant, and it is now COUNTED AND NAMED. A projection with no `abstract` section has no abstract paragraphs to classify, so it cannot contribute to the Methods/Results/Background/Conclusions counts. The topic is appended to `no_abstract` and printed with the denominator beside the object total, so a reader can reconcile `155 objects projected` against `131 of 155 Methods`. Measured at the time of baselining: 155 of 155 projections carry an abstract section, so the branch is currently unreached on every real object -- which is stated in the output rather than hidden, since a count that can only be zero is not evidence. Same shape as prove_no_value_lost.py:87 and lint_object_write_is_atomic.py:153.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/audit_analysis_population_estima: `if not n: continue` -- the absence IS the property meant, and it is now COUNTED AND NAMED. A trial row with no `nct` cannot be looked up in the registered-primary cache, so it cannot contribute a population token. On a sweep whose subject is whether an estimand can be established FROM THE REGISTRATION, a row carrying no registration id is the strongest instance of the thing being measured, and dropping it silently would remove exactly those rows from the denominator. The topic and the row's own id are appended to `unidentified` and printed beside the asked/read counts. Measured at baseline time: 4 rows, and they are NOT all defects -- `colchicine-cvd-coronary / ACTRN12614000093684` is a valid ANZCTR registration this cache cannot resolve because it queries ClinicalTrials.gov only, `cryptococcal-meningitis / ACTA` and `/ AMBITION-cm` are trial acronyms rather than ids, and `finerenone-review / NULLED:NCT01874431` is a deliberately nulled row. Naming them is what lets a reader tell a registry-coverage limit from a missing identity. Same shape as prove_no_value_lost.py:87 and prove_abstract_argument_is_never_composed.py:109.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/audit_p46_limbs_reach_a_reader.p: `if not p46.pooled_outcomes(obj): continue` DEFINES THE POPULATION and does not exclude anything from a fix. A topic with no pooled outcome has no limb whose delivery could be asked about -- P46's four limbs are all per-result or per-pooled-outcome. The count of topics that survive this line is PRINTED as the denominator of every figure the file reports, so the exclusion is visible in the output rather than silent.

`if not pages:` RECORDS A STATE, it does not skip. The limb is reported as NO PAGE, tallied, and the topics concerned are listed by name -- six of them reach no reader by any route, which is the single most consequential thing this instrument found. Turning the absence into a reported third state is the opposite of dropping it.

`if not pr:` RECORDS A STATE, it does not skip. A limb whose stored text contains no HTML-safe run of 40 characters cannot be searched for in escaped output without risking a FALSE ABSENCE, so it is reported as UNPROBEABLE and tallied separately from HELD ONLY. Reporting it as 'does not render' would be the accusing-direction error; reporting it as 'renders' would make the check unable to fail. It is currently 0 across the corpus.

baselined_with_reason.scripts/recount_second_assessor_after_d1: Skips a topic with no SECOND_ASSESSOR block. THE ABSENCE IS THE PROPERTY: a topic never given a second assessment has no disagreement rate to recount. NOT LEFT AS A BARE SKIP -- `seen_blocks` counts the topics that DO carry one, and the run exits PROOF FAILED if that count is zero, because a broken block lookup and a corpus with no second assessments read identically from inside the loop.

Skips a topic where no D1 judgement carries the `resolved_2026_08_21` marker. THIS IS THE DANGEROUS ONE AND IT IS WHY THE FLOOR EXISTS: if the marker name were spelled wrong -- the class-83 shape found six times in this run -- every topic would report `moved = 0`, the script would write nothing, print `0 topic(s) recounted` and exit 0. `seen_moved` counts topics with a moved D1 BEFORE the already-written skip, so the floor does not fire on an idempotent re-run, and the run exits PROOF FAILED if it is zero. Both directions were tested: the true state passes, and the same source with the marker renamed exits 1 naming the lookup rather than the corpus.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/build_paper_bookkeeping_2026_08_: Skips a topic with no pooled outcome. THE ABSENCE IS THE PROPERTY: this builder assembles references, an Introduction and the five PRISMA bookkeeping claims for a MANUSCRIPT, and a topic that pools nothing has no manuscript to build. The predicate is `p46_queue`'s own `pooled_outcomes`, the same one the P46 scorer and the delivery audit use, so this loop cannot silently disagree with them about which topics are in scope. NOT LEFT UNCOUNTED: the run exits PROOF FAILED if no topic passes, and the run that wrote this reported 28, which is the number the scorer reports.

rebaselined_2026_08_20: A BASELINE KEYED ON file:line CANNOT SURVIVE AN EDIT ABOVE THE LINE. Six-line docstring notes were added to lint_method_claim_has_a_field.py, lint_no_false_allclear.py and lint_self_describing_safety_claim.py recording that each had been PROVEN BY GRAFT. Every negative guard below those insertions shifted -- 217/220/227 -> 223/226/233, 102 -> 108, 74 -> 80 -- and re-read as NEW while the same number vanished as HEALED. Nine gone, eight new, and not one line of guard logic changed. THE KEY DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE THING IT NAMES, which is the same family as lint 50 storing a COUNT of claims rather than the claims: both detect movement and are blind to what moved. Keying on the guard text plus its enclosing function would survive an edit above it. Recorded, not fixed.

note_on_line_number_keys: This baseline is keyed by FILE:LINE, so any edit above a guard re-reports it as NEW. audit_p46_limbs_reach_a_reader.py's three guards have been re-baselined three times for that reason alone. The entries are now written by MATCHING THE LINE'S TEXT, not its position, because pairing reasons to positions produced an off-by-one set on the first attempt -- class 73, an entry misdescribing its own item.
rekeyed_2026_08_21: THE KEY CHANGED, THE POPULATION DID NOT. Entries were FILE:LINE, so any edit above a guard re-reported it as NEW; this file's own note records audit_p46_limbs_reach_a_reader.py being re-baselined THREE times for that alone, and a FOURTH re-baselining is what blocked the commit that prompted this. Re-writing the entries again would have been the symptom fix. Entries are now FILE::GUARD TEXT#nth-occurrence-in-that-file: stable when a line MOVES, still distinct when a duplicate line is ADDED. Three files carry an identical guard line twice today, which is why the occurrence index exists rather than a bare text key, and prove_ratchet now demonstrates the duplicate direction on every run. The old list held 154 entries against 140 guards actually present -- 14 named positions no longer occupied by any guard, the residue of previous re-keyings. Those are dropped: an entry that names nothing is not a suppression, it is noise that makes the ratchet look larger than the population it ratchets. Nothing present in the corpus at the moment of this rewrite was newly absorbed: the gate reported exactly 3 new guards, all three in audit_p46_limbs_reach_a_reader.py, all three pre-existing and merely shifted down 19 lines by an edit to refusal_named_in_section.
